focus: Convention-class producers and the cleanup pattern
noveltyJustification: Six findings are fully new (judge classes, census template-reading, cleanup rules, applied counts and second-run zeros, the no-frontmatter remainder, the coupling limit); one consolidates a known outcome and counts as half new.
ruledOut: Blaming the template-phrase producer for the GREP_CONVENTION remainder
Deleting author phrases to satisfy the judge

label: phrase-judge.mjs is the single verdict owner for phrase quality: generic workflow words, five frozen template-default sets (four phrases each), editor fallback words; it reports and gates but never rewrites an author-declared phrase because deleting one is a content decision the convention does not authorize.
template-phrase-census.mjs reads phrase blocks from the templates themselves so reports follow template edits, skips scratch and containment directories, and is read-only by design.

template-phrase-cleanup.mjs keeps an exact preview, writes only under --apply, imports its classifier from the census module, and (phase 12) handles partial blocks keeping author rows byte-for-byte, reseeds defaults-only lists, and trims trailing stop words with a create.sh-shared list pinned by a test.

The cleanup pair demonstrates the target properties: phase 11 applied to 509 files in 375 packets and a second dry run reported 0 files to change; phase 12 applied to 1,319 files across 541 folders and its second run also reported 0. Dry-run first, idempotent second run, operator-gated apply.

The remaining GREP_CONVENTION class is not template defaults (0 live carriers; 470 archive carriers left to phase 013): it is documents with no frontmatter block at all (tasks.md 22, plan.md 22, spec.md 12, implementation-summary.md 9, plus non-standard docs), single-token generic phrase warnings in decision-record.md, and uppercase basenames such as BENCHMARK-RELOCATED.md.

create.sh seeds all five documents with one slug phrase when the exact four-line template block is present, and the seeded-duplicate collision found in 3 packets was fixed in the tool so a hand fix cannot recur.

Phase 12's 21 already-failing packets show the coupling limit: they failed on rules the cleanup never touches (missing importance_tier/contextType, empty trigger lists, missing anchors, missing template headers), so phrase cleanup and structural repair are separate passes and a phrase-only heal would leave them red.

direction: Blaming template defaults for the persistent GREP_CONVENTION class
reason: The census reads templates themselves and reports zero live carriers; the remainder is old documents without frontmatter and non-conforming basenames.

direction: Deleting author phrases to satisfy the judge
reason: The judge refuses to rewrite author-declared phrases; doing so would violate the never-change-what-a-document-says constraint.
